cities.d: the capital and by far the largest city, crammed onto a small island and by some measures the world's densest city

x.around: Malé is small enough to walk around in an hour, and almost all sights are concentrated on the north shore, within a 15-min walk from the airport ferry.

hidden.d: Built in 1656 during the reign of Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar I, intricately carved with Arabic writings and ornamental patterns.

Mosque built in the 12th century by Dhovemi, the first Muslim king and founder of the Theemuge dynasty.

The sole surviving building of what was once the Sultan's palace is now the Maldivian National Museum, housing a scruffy, haphazard collection of royal regalia and old photographs, including three moon rocks and a faded Maldivian…
This little park, marked by a flagpole with a giant Maldivian flag, was the area where the events of 7 February 2012 led to the resignation of the president.

x.intro: Malé (މާލެ), pronounced Maa-leh, is the capital of Maldives. The city occupies the entire islet of Malé at the southern rim of North Malé Atoll. Malé is occasionally dismissed by travellers as a mere transit point with "nothing to do", and it is indeed not a party place.

next.d: the capital island of Alif Dhaal Atoll, 78 km (42 nautical miles) south-west of Malé

x.safe: Anti-government protests often turn into riots that are sometimes brutally suppressed by the government. Avoid participating in protests or political activism.

cities.d: the Maldives' second city in the far south of the archipelago, the former capital of the short-lived United Suvadive Republic

x.around: The four islands of Gan, Feydhoo, Maradhoo and Hithadhoo are connected to each other by causeways. There is a bus service which runs daily every two hours (except on Friday morning) all the way from the Gan island up to the north of the Hithadhoo island and back. The bus is reliable but slow: the 15-km-long route takes almost an hour.

hidden.d: Was founded in 2013 on Maradhoo Island, Addu Atoll. It’s a local island in the southernmost atoll of the Maldives. Aquaventure is the first PADI Dive Center in Local Addu, where a full range of daily excursions and PADI courses…

x.intro: Addu (also Seenu) is the southernmost atoll in the Maldives. Hithadhoo, its capital, was the base of the short-lived United Suvadive Republic secessionist movement in 1959–1963.

intro: The Maldives (Dhivehi: ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ Dhivehi Raajje) are a chain of low-lying coral islands in the Indian Ocean with picture-perfect beaches, strikingly blue water, and luxury resorts. There are 200 inhabited islands and 165 islands with tourist resorts. Just under the surface of the beautiful blue ocean, there's a wealth of wildlife to see: over 2000 species of fish in all colours of the rainbow roam the clear waters around the islands.

other.d: one of the inhabited islands of Lhaviyani Atoll

x.around: Kuredu is one of the larger tourist islands in the Maldives, but you can still walk around its circumference (along the beach) in 40 minutes to 1 hour.
x.intro: Kuredu (Kurendhoo) is an island located in the Lhaviyani Atoll of the Maldives.

other.d: island belonging to North Ari Atoll

x.intro: Mathiveri is a small island that belongs to North Ari atoll, Maldives. Only 900 people live there.

next.d: Rasdhoo, Feridhoo, Maalhos, Himandhoo — all of these Atif atoll islands can be reached by ferry from Mathiveri

other.d: smallish inhabited island and the capital of the North Ari Atoll

x.intro: Rasdhoo is a smallish island with 850 citizens and a capital of Alif Alif Atoll (or North Ari Atoll), Maldives.

next.d: isolated island north of Atif atoll
Bodufulhadhoo, Mathiveri, Feridhoo, Maalhos, Himandhoo — all of these Atif atoll islands can be reached by ferry from Rasdhoo

other.d: an isolated inhabited island that administratively belongs to North Ari Atoll. It's also the largest producer of watermelon in Maldives.

x.intro: Thoddoo is an isolated inhabited island that administratively belongs to North Ari atoll, Maldives. It's quite large by Maldivian standards, it will take about an hour to circumvent it. In 2014, it had a population of about 1,500 people (including foreigners).

next.d: capital of the North Ari atoll and the closest inhabited island accessible by ferry
Bodufulhadhoo, Mathiveri, Feridhoo, Maalhos, Himandhoo — all of these Atif atoll islands can be reached by ferry from Thoddoo

other.d: smallish 1 km long island of Alif Alif Atoll

x.around: The island is tiny and thus the only available means of transportation is by foot. You can walk around the island in less than half an hour. Sometimes there are large puddles, especially during rainy season when one has to be careful standing on them as they tend to be very slippery.

hidden.d: The biggest isolated rock in the Maldives. This limestone islet is about 15 m (50 feet) long, 8 m (25 feet) wide, and about 1½ m (5 feet) from the water’s edge, It is the only part of Alif atoll that is above water, and it's a…

This is a small uninhabited island with three grown trees in the middle. It's covered by white sands and washed by turquoise water with stunning underwater beauty. There are no toilets, bars or rooms.

x.intro: Ukulhas (Dhivehi: އުކުޅަސް) island is one of the inhabited islands of North Ari Atoll in the Maldives. The island has only been a travel destination since 2012; therefore, it has just a couple of inns and is somewhat hard to get to. Hence, if you enjoy diving, fishing and swimming without a crowd of fellow tourists, Ukulhas might be the destination you're looking for.
